newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Fieldwork slows movement.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Fieldwork slows movement.

text.p: Movement of hard red winter wheat has slowed in recent days as open, dry conditions have allowed farmers to work in their fields, grain merchandisers in the U.S. Plains said Tuesday.
"A lot of guys out west are busy planting corn so they don't have time to come to the elevator and sell anything," a south-central Kansas dealer said.
The drop in KCBT HRW wheat futures prices Monday also proved a disincentive to sell, dealers said.
KCBT May wheat closed down 21 cents at $4.49, and new crop July wheat lost 12 cents per bushel to settle at $4.41.

The weekly state crop reports released Monday afternoon showed mixed assessments of the U.S. HRW wheat crop. Further deterioration in the Texas and Oklahoma crops was offset by improved ratings for the Kansas crop.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: K=KCBT May wheat futures. N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
